notes:
Quick snapshot: Helmstone is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for latency-sensitive customer-facing chat and internal retrieval. Primary driver is predictable unit economics for 24/7 mission-critical inference and avoiding variable hosted costs. CTO said: 'We need hard numbers to justify a 6–12 month commit — show us break-even with utilization bands.'

POC & perf highlights:
- POC kickoff 2026-02-22 (throughput + latency runbook)
- Perf run 2026-03-04: target traffic mix simulated (40% chat, 50% embeddings, 10% rerank)
- Observed p50/p95 generation latency on baseline model: 55ms / 140ms (single-query, pre-warm), peak concurrency test sustained 4200 req/min at p95 ~185ms when cold KV cache hits drop
- KV/prefix cache projected to reduce token generation by ~18-24% for typical dialog flows

Cost-model summary shared 2026-03-10 (v1):
- Workload inputs: avg tokens per chat turn = 220 tokens outbound, 80 tokens inbound; avg embeddings request = 1536 dims, ~768 tokens processed; estimated peak QPS = 20 req/s (aggregate)
- Baseline reserved hardware candidates discussed: 4x H100-80GB nodes vs 8x A100-40GB nodes (different rack/network implications).
- Unit economics (modeling assumptions): reserved capacity rate = vendor-provided (Redwood committed-capacity price) -> modeled effective infra cost per GPU-hour = $6.50 (H100 reserved blended) after commit credits; variable hosting (on-demand) equivalent = $12.40/hr.
- Utilization bands modeled: conservative 40% / expected 65% / aggressive 85% — sensitivity across 6, 12, 24 month commit lengths.
- Token-level math (example):
  * At 65% util, amortized infra + ops + SW = $0.00058/token generated (includes network egress, monitoring, and 10% buffer for peak).
  * At 40% util, same stack = $0.00102/token.
  * On hosted API baseline (no commit) equivalent observed = $0.00135/token (including per-request overhead).
- Caching & batching recommendations reduce effective per-token cost by 12-20% in most steady-state charts; recommend prefix caching for chat to capture saved KV ops.

Negotiation & SLA asks from Helmstone:
- 6-month initial commit with option to convert unused commit to credits toward Dedicated+Optimize services.
- Latency SLO target: p95 inference < 150ms across US regions; request for 99.9% availability and 99.95% for critical endpoints.
- Credit policy: 5% service credit per 30 min failure window beyond SLA, capped at 50% monthly invoice.
- Right-sizing clause: quarterly re-baselining with one downward step allowed after first 90 days (requires 30-day notice).
- Data residency: primary US-east with DR in US-west; no EU residency requirement for this project but will be a blocker for certain customers.

Open items (actionables):
- Redwood to produce revised cost model (v2) with: region-specific GPU pricing, explicit SLO credit language, and 6-mo vs 12-mo blended ARR scenarios (due 2026-03-18).
- Helmstone to provide a conservative 12-month traffic forecast (week-of-2026-03-22) and a 90-day pilot acceptance checklist.
- Security to complete SOC2 questionnaire + KMS integration plan (owner: Priya).

Sales hints / conversational notes:
- Finance is highly cost-savvy; show step-function savings at >=60% utilization.
- CTO is skeptical of vendor lock — emphasize ability to pin model versions and export logs/disk snapshots.
- They like the Optimize toolkit: ask how quantization profiles + batching recommendations will be operationalized during POC.
